feedback.problem:
Consider the equation in the variable $u,$ given by

$$
5ru+3=2u+6
$$

where $r$ is a constant. Given that this equation has no solution, what is the value of $r?$

$r=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose we have an equation of the form

$$
ax=b
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are constants, and $b\ne 0.$ If $a=0,$ then the equation has no solution.

First, we rewrite the equation in the form $au=b.$ 

We start by subtracting $2u$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5ru+3 & =2u+6 \\ 5ru-2u+3 & =2u+6-2u \\ 5ru-2u+3 & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we subtract $3$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}5ru-2u+3 & =6 \\ 5ru-2u+3-3 & =6-3 \\ 5ru-2u & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we factor $u$ on the left-hand side. This gives

$$
(5r-2)u=3.
$$

Notice that this equation is now in the form $au=b:$

$$
{{(5r-2)}_{⏟}}_{a}u={{3}_{⏟}}_{b}
$$

Therefore, the equation has no solution if

$$
5r-2=0.
$$

Solving this for $r,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5r-2 & =0 \\ 5r-2+2 & =0+2 \\ 5r & =2 \\ \frac{5r}{5} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ r & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
